title: Driver-placed claims get a lease capped at the dispatch deadline (#879)

story.i_want_to: a claim placed for a runner dispatch to expire at the dispatch's deadline
story.so_that: a killed session releases its story within minutes, not 23 hours, and no other claimant is affected

rationale: The lease is one global 24h value against a 3600s wall clock, so a killed session holds its story for most of a day, and lowering the global value breaks every non-runner claimant. A per-claim cap for the population the runner hard-kills fixes that, and sharing the same instant with the runner is what keeps a re-contracted story from running under two sessions.

acceptance_criteria.description: Progress.claim_story/3 accepts lease_until:, and a claim taken with it stores stories.claim_lease_cap and sets claimed_until to that value.
Placement claims with lease_until = placed_at + wall_clock_seconds + DISPATCH_LEASE_GRACE_SECONDS.
Renewing a claim with a claim_lease_cap sets claimed_until to the earlier of now + claim_lease_seconds() and the cap.
A claim taken without lease_until, through claim_story/3 or bulk_claim/4, keeps claimed_until = now + claim_lease_seconds() and a nil claim_lease_cap.
The application refuses to start when DISPATCH_LEASE_GRACE_SECONDS is below Capacity.release_grace_seconds/0.
The implement dispatch payload carries deadline_at equal to the claim's claim_lease_cap.
The renew_story_claim tool description and its mcp-server/README.md row state that a driver-placed claim is capped at its dispatch deadline.
